Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 10 February 2025
Patient: Beatrice Hall, aged 42

Dear colleague,

Beatrice attended our clinic for routine annual review. She has an established diagnosis of focal epilepsy with impaired awareness, which has been well characterized since 2021.

Her seizure frequency remains entirely stable on carbamazepine modified-release 400 mg twice daily, which she takes regularly without significant adverse effects. Over the past year she has continued to experience roughly one focal seizure per month. Her most recent focal seizure occurred on 28 January 2025. She describes a brief epigastric sensation followed by confusion lasting one to two minutes. She has had no generalized tonic-clonic convulsions and reports no other event types.

We agreed to make no changes to her carbamazepine dosage. No additional medications or investigations are required at this time. We will arrange routine follow-up in six months.

Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 15 August 2025
Patient: Beatrice Hall

Dear colleague,

I reviewed Beatrice in clinic today. Her diagnosis remains focal epilepsy with impaired awareness.

Her clinical pattern is unchanged. She continues carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily with good compliance. She continues to experience approximately one focal seizure per month, with the latest episode on 2 August 2025. There have been no tonic-clonic convulsions, nocturnal attacks, or new semiologies since our last review in February.

Her medication is maintained at the current dose. No investigations were requested. We will see her again for routine follow-up in approximately six months.

Administrative follow-up letter
Consultation slot: 20 November 2025
Patient: Beatrice Hall

The patient could not attend today. We have sent a replacement appointment. No clinical history was obtained, no medication reconciliation was performed, and this letter records no assessment or investigation update.
